[b]Emergency Statement from the Minister of Defense Fazel Al-Moin[/b]

The Government of Greater Tirakan addresses the nation and the international community regarding a grave act of aggression that occurred in the early hours of this morning, the 9th of January.
At approximately 02:17 local time, the Karzeh Valley electrical substation, located within the sovereign territory of Greater Tirakan near the Shahbani border, was deliberately sabotaged. The facility, which supplies electricity to over 180,000 civilians across three districts, shows coordinated structural damage through, what seems to be, military-grade demolition.

The consequences were immediate. Critical power distribution failed, forcing several hospitals onto emergency generators. A large portion of the local transportation systems were disrupted, blocking traffic, civilian communication networks temporarily collapsed, leaving many citizen without connection to the outer world. Most tragically, twenty-eight Tiraki citizens lost their lives, including eight border patrol soldiers, responding to the attack and two first-response technicians who were attempting to restore service under these fragile conditions. Due to the collapsed traffic systems, an unknown amount of residents requiring emergency service, did not recieve help in time, including the 76-year old Ana Afhlak, which passed away, with the ambulance taking over 40 minutes to arrive, having no chance of performing cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

Our analysis, conducted by the Ministry of Defense and the TIS, has found critical evidence regarding the perpetrators. Surveillance footage retrieved from security cameras, partially damaged but recoverable, shows armed soldiers in Shahbani uniforms. Emergency calls from local residents describe uniformed individuals moving in tactical formation prior to the explosion. Equipment traces and tactical signatures observed at the scene, correspond to Shahbani military units currently stationed along our border.
These findings are not speculative. The attack was deliberate and coordinated.

Shahban is known to breaching the spirit of prior understandings between our states, but they have now stepped over the red line. Over the past months, Greater Tirakan has sought diplomatic dialogue despite tensions coming from territorial expansion and treaty violations by Shahban. We have repeatedly expressed willingness to reinforce agreements and de-escalate their one-sided border militarization. Those attempts and requests for compromise were rejected. Trust has already been strained for long enough.
The sabotage of civilian infrastructure and the deaths of Tiraki citizens represent a crossing of a line that we can not ignore.

The Republic of Greater Tirakan hereby issues a formal ultimatum to the Emirate of Shahban:

First, Shahban must immediately identify and surrender the personnel responsible for the Karzeh Valley substation attack. These individuals are to be transferred into Tiraki custody and subjected to lawful proceedings before Tiraki courts.

Second, Shahban must provide full financial compensation for the destruction inflicted, including infrastructure reconstruction costs and reparations to the families of the deceased.

Third, Shahban must initiate verifiable demilitarization measures along our shared border. This includes the withdrawal of all forward-positioned combat units, that currently threaten Tiraki civilian zones.

These demands represent the minimum required to restore stability and prevent further escalation. We do not seek war or confrontation for its own sake. Yet, no responsible government can permit cross-border sabotage of civilian infrastructure without response.
Should Shahban refuse to comply with these reasonable and necessary measures, Greater Tirakan will take all actions required to protect its citizen and drive Shahban out of their illegitimately claimed territory, by taking down the people responsible for this awful decision.

We expect a formal response within 24 hours, before action will be taken.

The responsibility for what follows rests entirely with those who chose to bring violence across our border.

-- Pings --

[b]January 16, 2028: Order 28-1[/b]
[i]Internal SCSID Decree: Published to legislators and media by the SCSID[/i]
Whereas the political fervor of the revolutionaries has been quelled by the strong leadership of Polenne Strømm, the SCSID sees it fit that the state should establish and re-organise the national prison system to repatriate former enemies of the state and former criminals. 

It is hereby declared that under this order (28-1) a new prison and the first of its kind shall be opened for the benefit of society, wherein the prison shall be focused on producing strong and glorious citizens, and it shall remind the enemies of Rosenmarkke both inside and outside that the state is merciful in its dealings and that none should be banished from society if they are only to accept and learn from their ways and repent fully. 

The prison shall be open 24/7 for tours of the working conditions and workplace ethics, hosted by tour guides, and shall have a capacity for 10,000 prisoners. The prison is to be named The Polenne Strømm Center For Rehabilitation[/b]

Glory to Rosenmarkke.

[b][u]Dhora Officers Make Their Leave[/u][/b]

Understanding that war is imminent between Shahban and Tirakan, the Dhora Ministry of Defence recalled all officers sent to Tirakan to train their SAM crews. The public announcement was deceptive. While the Il-76s that brought the officers did come back to Dhornaper with some of the officers, the Ministry of Defence left behind enough to operate a SAM brigade.

The secretly formed 1st Missileers brigade and it's 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Missileer battalions were manned with the officers of one of Dhoranaper's own SAM brigades. The officers, with ten years of experience operating and training with the Pantsirs and P-18 radars, would operate independently of Tirakan's command chain but in coordination with Tirakan's military. Their primary objective would be to cover the most likely approaches of Shahban's aircraft to Tirakan's capital.

Per the Secret agreement between Dhornaper and Tirakan, the 1st Missileer brigade requisitioned three of the Pantsirs given to Tirakan and one of the P-18 radars, leaving 37 Pantsirs and three P-18s for Tirakan's military. Alongside this, they also requisitioned 15 radar imitators and three inflatable decoys.

At night, after checking the equipment, they quickly evacuated for their preplanned positions to the west of Tirakan's capital, near the forests. They inflated the decoys and drove without headlights for their positions before setting up their Pantsirs, P-18, and radar imitators, field landlines to communicate with Tirkan's military without eavesdropping, camouflaging their equipment, and preparing themselves mentally for the coming war.

While the 1st Missileers are veterans, they'll need to depend on Tirakan's logistics for supplies and ammunition and on clear lines of communication between their units and Tirakan's military.

[b]Bascover Invited to the Four Eyes Agreement[/b]
[i]By unanimous vote, the Republic of [nation]Bascover[/nation] has been invited to the Four Eyes Agreement (now the Five Eyes) as a full member of the treaty. Pending the signing of the treaty, Bascover will be obliged to act in the interests of the four main pillars of the treaty, which are as follows:

[list=1][*]Intelligence: partnership nations will agree to work together in coordinating counterintelligence efforts against hostile forces, while sharing any information they may have that is imperative to ensuring the security of the Argos region is maintained

[*]Standardisation: Partnership nations will agree to use the same ammunition types for ease of trading technology

[*]Advanced capability: partnership nations will agree to share military technology with one another that promotes the advancement of the following fields:
[list=a][*]Submarine warfare
[*]Quantum technology
[*]Cyber warfare/Cybersecurity
[*]Hypersonic capability
[*]Long-distance strike capability[/list]

[*]Non-Aggression: Partnership nations agree to not engage in any form of aggression against one another.[/list]

We await the reply from the delegation of Bascover, and sincerely hope they choose to join the treaty. A cooperative Argos is a safe and strong Argos.[/i]

[quote=new_westmore;61309223]
Rahat leans back. [i]"Good to hear it then, brother. See you in three weeks. Do not disappoint me."[/i] Rahat then whacks Hamza across the head with the butt of his handgun, knocking him out cold.

When Hamza awakes, he is back in the alleyway where Rahat's goons ambushed him. Rain is pouring down from the murky night sky above him.[/quote]
His brown hair sticks to his olive skin, and his beard is soaked with water droplets falling onto his slightly bloodied coat. He is cold, but he is alive, unlike the Cartel. Though he is not a true practitioner, he gives thanks to God. Perhaps... Perhaps this is a new lease on life? Nah. 

He remains in the alley, finding whatever shelter he can for a time, while he searches for a motel online to stay at for a few days, while he organises the shipment of as much Opium and Arms as they can muster, the best quality they can get past security. He eventually finds one and makes his way towards it. 

Like all things in Brunswick, it's grimy, dirty and cheap. He speaks to the clerk; the nature of his heritage ensures he remains partially disturbed by the unveiled woman. He shrugs it off, prejudices to get over if he is to live here and profit here. 

He began to speak, [i]"Pa-"[/i] He stopped himself. If conversing with Rahat has taught him anything, then the locals do not speak as eloquently as he. [i]"You got a room? I have cash."[/i]

The older woman looked him up and down, [i]"We do, room 27 upstairs if you're interested."[/i] Her eyes tried to make out what tribe he came from, Shamatine of course, but which sandhole?

Hamza felt unnerved. [i]"Yeah, yeah that'll do."[/i] He placed an amount of cash on the table and made his way to the room. Within, he prepared certain countermeasures for a break-in should one occur. He would then proceed to make contact with the powers-that-be.
